{"node_id":"NRS_484B_560_7a","law_refs":["NRS-484B-560-7a"],"subject":{"binder":"x","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"It is unlawful for the driver of any vehicle:","role":"subject"},{"id":"s2","text":"When crossing at grade any track or tracks of a railroad,","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s3","text":"to fail to completely cross the track or tracks without stopping","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s4","text":"due to insufficient: (1) Space for the vehicle on the opposite side of the railroad crossing;","role":"condition"},{"id":"s5","text":"or (2) Undercarriage clearance of the vehicle.","role":"condition"},{"id":"s6","text":"As used in this section, “completely cross” means to travel across a railroad track or tracks in such a manner that the trailing end of the vehicle is 15 feet or more past the nearest rail of the railroad track or tracks.","role":"definitional"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', less the devices it excepts), claimed as one atom and never expanded into classes. 'the driver of' names who controls that vehicle, a relational role and no membership, read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency). The aggregate's 'not a stand-in' clause excludes a relational role as membership, which is why 'driver' claims nothing of its own."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["st.railway_crossing","rel.occupies","st.region_geometry"],"derived":[],"justification":"st.railway_crossing is the 'level crossing of a railway with the roadway, and its nearest rail': 'crossing at grade any track or tracks' is a crossing on the level. DEF-NRS-484A-200 makes a railroad 'a carrier of persons or property upon cars, other than streetcars, operated upon stationary rails'; the atom's contract is a crossing of a railway with the roadway, which a streetcar track laid along the street is not, so the definition's exclusion is already the contract's. 'When crossing' anchors the crossing to x: rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') while x is on the crossing, and st.region_geometry ('the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it') after its footprint has left it, until x has completely crossed (s6). rel.occupies is read only as overlap; st.region_geometry's 'not a stand-in for occupancy' is respected, since the distance is read only past the crossing, beside the occupancy that x had before."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["st.railway_crossing","rel.occupies","st.region_geometry","dev.human_direction","dev.governs","st.travel_region","prim.closest_approach_within","prim.closest_approach_distance"],"derived":["drv.motion.stopped"],"justification":"'without stopping' is read with DEF-NRS-484A-260, the definition that applies: 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not' is drv.motion.stopped, the halt at one observation, which denotes the halt 'whoever or whatever controls the road user' and holds at a momentary halt because it reads the one observation. The definition's exclusions are not the concept's and the rule carries them beside it: 'except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic' by prim.closest_approach_within and prim.closest_approach_distance, another road user's predicted closest approach to x within the conflict horizon coming within the conflict clearance; 'in compliance with the directions of a police officer' by dev.human_direction ('a person directing traffic and the direction given', role police_officer, indication stop) governing (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') a travel region (st.travel_region) x occupies (rel.occupies). dev.governs' 'not a stand-in for a position' is respected: it is read only as which region the officer's direction controls. 'fail to completely cross the track or tracks' reads the crossing of s2 and the law's own definition (s6): the halt is forbidden while x is on the crossing (rel.occupies) or less than the stated distance past it (st.region_geometry)."},{"span":"s4","atoms":["rel.bearing","rel.surface_gap"],"derived":[],"justification":"'due to insufficient ... Space for the vehicle on the opposite side' states why the halt happens and is read through the conduct it explains (observable_reading, purpose): x halts with another road user directly ahead of it, the one taking the space beyond the crossing. rel.bearing is the 'direction of b from a in a's frame', whose longitudinal component positive places y ahead of x, on the side toward which x crosses; rel.surface_gap, the 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies', at most the queue standstill gap says x stands at the back of y as a queued vehicle does, so the space x needed is taken. rel.surface_gap has no 'not a stand-in' clause; rel.bearing is read as a direction, not a distance. The words name no class for what fills the space, so y is any road user other than x."},{"span":"s6","atoms":["st.railway_crossing","st.region_geometry","rel.occupies"],"derived":[],"justification":"The law's own definition of 'completely cross': 'the trailing end of the vehicle is 15 feet or more past the nearest rail'. st.region_geometry gives 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it', so once x is past the crossing its body's nearest point to the crossing, the trailing end, is at least the stated literal from the crossing's boundary; 'past' is read as x having occupied the crossing (rel.occupies) and left it without the distance reaching the literal since, so the trailing end lies beyond the crossing on the side x crossed to. st.railway_crossing carries the crossing 'and its nearest rail', the boundary the distance is read to (reading on s3)."}],"operationalizations":[],"assumptions":[{"span":"s5","id":"asm.undercarriage_grounded","meaning":"The underside of the road user's vehicle touches, or lacks the clearance to pass over, the surface it is travelling across at the observation."}],"intentions":[],"compositions":[],"residues":[],"binders":[{"name":"x","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}],"applicability":"x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) crossing a railway crossing at grade: there is a railway crossing r (st.railway_crossing) whose region x's footprint overlaps at the observation (rel.occupies), or overlapped at an earlier observation with x's body less than the s6 literal (15 ft) from r (st.region_geometry distance) at every observation since that one: since(distance(x, r) < 15 ft, occupies(x, r)). A vehicle that halts short of a crossing it has not entered is not crossing; one whose body has reached the literal distance past the crossing has completely crossed and is no longer crossing.","obligation":"Violated at an observation where, for a railway crossing r selected as in the applicability (bound again in the obligation with the whole selection: the crossing x occupies, or occupied with its body less than the literal from it at every observation since), x is halted (drv.motion.stopped, tolerance p.motion_speed_tolerance) and the halt is due to an insufficiency the words name: (1) some road user y other than x lies ahead of x (rel.bearing from x to y, longitudinal component positive) with the gap between their bodies (rel.surface_gap) at most p.queue_standstill_gap, or (2) the declared assumption asm.undercarriage_grounded holds; unless the halt is one the stopping definition excludes: some road user z other than x has a predicted closest approach to x within p.conflict_time_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance), or a dev.human_direction with role police_officer and indication stop governs (dev.governs) a travel region (st.travel_region) x occupies (rel.occupies). Compliant at every other observation of the crossing: crossing without halting, or halting only once completely across, meets the duty. Where x is halted on the crossing with no road user ahead within the gap and the assumption undeclared, the cause of the halt is unknown and so is the verdict.","params":["p.motion_speed_tolerance","p.queue_standstill_gap","p.conflict_time_horizon","p.conflict_centre_clearance"],"narrowings":[{"span":"s1","why":"'the driver of any vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"agency"},{"span":"s4","why":"'due to insufficient ... Space' states why the halt happens; it is read through the conduct it explains, the halt directly behind a road user standing ahead within the queue standstill gap, not through a cause the trace cannot show.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"purpose"},{"span":"s3","why":"'the nearest rail' is read as the rail nearest the vehicle's trailing end once it has crossed, the edge of the crossing region on the side it crosses to, so a vehicle whose body is still on a further track has not completely crossed; the distance is read to the crossing region's boundary as the source maps it.","kind":"reading"},{"span":"s3","why":"The stopping definition's exclusion 'in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device' is read for the officer only: a device directs a halt at the place it marks (its stop line, or short of the crossing), and a halt on the tracks or less than the stated distance past them is not at such a place, so no device's indication excuses it; 'other traffic' in the definition is read as every other road user of the scene.","kind":"reading"}],"scenarios":[{"name":"forbid","expected":"violated","narrative":"x, a car, enters a level crossing; a truck y stands queued just beyond it. x halts behind y with its body still on the tracks, the gap to y within the standstill gap; no officer directs traffic and no road user moves toward x."},{"name":"permit","expected":"compliant","narrative":"x, alone in the scene, drives over a level crossing at a steady speed and continues well past it without halting."},{"name":"idle","expected":"not_applicable","narrative":"x drives on a road with no railway crossing and halts behind a queued vehicle."},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"x halts on the crossing with a vehicle y ahead of it; the source declares rel.surface_gap absent and the trace declares no undercarriage assumption, so whether x halts at the back of a queue is unknown.","masked":["rel.surface_gap"]},{"name":"branch_1","expected":"compliant","narrative":"x crosses without halting and halts behind queued y only once its body is farther than the stated distance past the crossing."},{"name":"branch_2","expected":"violated","narrative":"x halts on the crossing with no road user ahead of it; the trace declares asm.undercarriage_grounded for x at that observation."},{"name":"branch_3","expected":"compliant","narrative":"As in forbid, but a police officer at the crossing directs x to stop (dev.human_direction, role police_officer, indication stop, governing the lane x occupies) when it halts."}],"literals":[{"span":"s6","text":"15 feet","value":15,"unit":"ft"}],"param_proposals":[],"gaps":[]}
{"node_id":"NRS_484B_600_1a","law_refs":["NRS-484B-600-1a"],"subject":{"binder":"x","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"b1","text":"It is unlawful for any person to drive or operate","role":"obligation"},{"id":"b2","text":"a vehicle of any kind or character at:","role":"subject"},{"id":"b3","text":"A rate of speed greater than is reasonable or proper, having due regard for the traffic, surface and width of the highway, the weather and other highway conditions.","role":"standard"}],"elements":[{"span":"b1","atoms":[],"derived":["drv.motion.moving"],"justification":"'to drive or operate' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: drv.motion.moving, 'a road user is in motion at the observation ... whoever or whatever controls the road user'; a vehicle at rest has no rate of speed the standard could find unreasonable. 'any person' names who controls the vehicle, a role read through the vehicle's conduct (observable_reading, agency)."},{"span":"b2","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', less the devices it excepts), one atom, never expanded; 'of any kind or character' adds no class beyond the definition's."}],"operationalizations":[{"span":"b3","standard":"A rate of speed greater than is reasonable or proper, having due regard for the traffic, surface and width of the highway, the weather and other highway conditions","concepts":["kin.speed","drv.motion.stopping_distance","ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic","rel.ahead_behind_in_lane","rel.surface_gap","env.wet_road","env.ice_or_snow","env.precipitation","env.visibility","st.sight_distance","st.curvature","st.lane","st.lane_width","rel.occupies","kin.extent"],"params":["p.perception_reaction_time","p.surface_friction_accel_dry","p.surface_friction_accel_wet","p.surface_friction_accel_ice_or_snow","p.following_min_time_headway","p.lane_keeping_margin_per_speed"],"convention":"Stopping-sight-distance model (AASHTO Green Book): a speed is reasonable only where the vehicle can halt, after a perception-reaction time and at the deceleration the surface sustains, within the distance it can see along the road (st.sight_distance) and through the air (env.visibility); the surface selects that deceleration (ice or snow, else a wet road or falling precipitation, else dry). Traffic: time-headway convention, the speed times the minimum time headway within the gap to each road user of the traffic ahead in the lane. Other highway conditions: the lateral acceleration in a bend (speed squared times st.curvature) within the acceleration the surface sustains. Width: time-to-line-crossing convention, the speed times the lateral margin needed per unit of speed within the free lateral margin, half of the lane width less the vehicle width. Each measured magnitude enters its bound, so the bound moves with the speed, the gap, the distances, the curvature and the width; the surface condition selects among bounds.","surrogate":true}],"assumptions":[],"intentions":[],"compositions":[],"residues":[],"binders":[{"name":"x","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}],"applicability":"x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that is being driven: x is in motion (drv.motion.moving, tolerance p.motion_speed_tolerance).","obligation":"Surrogate. Let a be the surface's deceleration: p.surface_friction_accel_ice_or_snow where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.surface_friction_accel_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, else p.surface_friction_accel_dry; the stopping distance SD is drv.motion.stopping_distance(x; p.perception_reaction_time, a), written as a Term.cond over the three calls, each with its own constant parameter. (1) SD is at most the sight distance at x's place (st.sight_distance) and at most the visibility distance (env.visibility). (2) For every road user y of the traffic (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) that is ahead of x in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane), x's speed times p.following_min_time_headway is at most the gap between their bodies (rel.surface_gap). (3) x's speed squared times the curvature at x's place (st.curvature) is at most a, selected as above. (4) For every lane l (st.lane) x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), x's speed times p.lane_keeping_margin_per_speed is at most half of the difference between the lane's width (st.lane_width) and x's width (kin.extent, width). oncoming, crossing and adjacent-lane traffic, and traffic on a way with no mapped lane, set no bound.","kind":"reading"},{"span":"b3","why":"'surface' is read through env.wet_road and env.ice_or_snow, which select the deceleration; wind and temperature are not read.","kind":"reading"},{"span":"b3","why":"The catch-all 'other highway conditions' is read only through st.sight_distance and st.curvature; grade, works and other conditions are not read.","kind":"reading"}],"scenarios":[{"name":"forbid","expected":"violated","narrative":"x, alone in the scene, drives on a dry road in dense fog at a speed whose stopping distance far exceeds the visibility distance."},{"name":"permit","expected":"compliant","narrative":"x, alone in the scene, drives at a moderate speed on a dry, straight road with wide lanes in clear weather and a long sight distance; every other bound is met."}],"literals":[],"param_proposals":[{"name":"p.perception_reaction_time","unit":"s","value":2.5,"convention":"Brake reaction time of the stopping-sight-distance model: the time from sighting a need to halt to applying the brakes, chosen to cover most drivers.","source":"AASHTO, A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets (Green Book), stopping sight distance"},{"name":"p.surface_friction_accel_dry","unit":"m/s²","value":3.4,"convention":"Deceleration of the stopping-sight-distance model, which most drivers achieve and most paved surfaces sustain when dry; also read as the acceleration a dry surface sustains in a bend.","source":"AASHTO Green Book, stopping sight distance deceleration rate"},{"name":"p.surface_friction_accel_wet","unit":"m/s²","value":2.5,"convention":"Deceleration a wet paved surface sustains: a wet-pavement friction coefficient of about a quarter at highway speeds, times gravity; {"concept_id":"drv.motion.stopping_distance","kind":"quantity","contract":"The distance a road user would travel from the observation to a halt if it kept its current speed for a reaction time and then slowed at a constant deceleration: its speed at the observation (kin.speed) times `reaction_time`, plus the square of that speed divided by twice `decel`, in metres along its path. It is a quantity of the road user's own motion at the one observation, whoever or whatever controls it, and is zero for a road user standing still. Not denoted: the distance an actual later halt takes; the grade or the surface, which the caller states through the deceleration it passes.","definition":null,"args":[{"name":"x","sort":"track"}],"params":[{"name":"reaction_time","unit":"s","meaning":"the time the road user keeps its speed before it begins to slow"},{"name":"decel","unit":"m/s²","meaning":"the constant rate at which it slows once it begins to; strictly positive"}],"elements":[{"span":"its speed at the observation (kin.speed)","atoms":["kin.speed"],"concepts":[],"justification":"kin.speed is the 'magnitude of velocity' in m/s; the distance to a halt depends on that magnitude alone, so neither the direction of motion nor the heading is read."}],"residues":[],"literals":[{"value":2,"unit":"count","why":"The kinematic factor of constant deceleration: the distance to halt from a speed is the square of the speed over twice the deceleration."}],"scenarios":[{"name":"holds","expected":"compliant","narrative":"A road user moves at a steady speed; the instance's bounds bracket its speed times the reaction time plus the square of its speed over twice the deceleration, read at that observation."},{"name":"fails","expected":"violated","narrative":"The same road user; the instance's bounds lie wholly below the value the contract computes."},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"The source declares kin.speed absent; the value is unknown.","masked":["kin.speed"]}],"used_by":["NRS_484B_600_1a","NRS_484D_215_1_o1"],"supersedes":null}

The manner borrowed from DEF-NRS-484B-420 ('extended horizontally') is the posture whose meaning the source reads into sig.hand_signal. sig.turn_indicator's 'not a stand-in for the turn itself' is respected: the lamp is read as a signal, never as the turn.","source_spans":["c6"]},{"span":"c7","atoms":["sig.hand_signal"],"derived":[],"justification":"The exception permits a second posture for one meaning: a right-turn signal given 'by extending his or her right hand and arm horizontally and to the right side'. sig.hand_signal carries the meaning of the arm signal given, right, whichever arm and posture give it, so the right-arm signal and the posture the borrowed manner states both read as meaning right and both meet the duty."}],"operationalizations":[],"assumptions":[],"intentions":[],"compositions":[{"span":"c6","as":"definition","source":"DEF-NRS-484B-420","quote":"extended horizontally"}],"residues":[],"binders":[{"name":"x","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle","ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle","ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter"]}],"applicability":"x is a bicycle, an electric bicycle or an electric scooter (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-025::bicycle, or DEF-NRS-484B-017::electric_bicycle, or DEF-NRS-484B-018::electric_scooter) whose footprint overlaps a roadway r (rel.occupies, st.roadway) at the observation.","obligation":"At the observation, every turn signal x gives is given by hand and arm: where x's turn indicator (sig.turn_indicator) shows left, x's arm signal (sig.hand_signal) has meaning left, and where it shows right, x's arm signal has meaning right. {"node_id":"NRS_484B_560_7a","law_refs":["NRS-484B-560-7a"],"subject":{"binder":"x","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"It is unlawful for the driver of any vehicle:","role":"subject"},{"id":"s2","text":"When crossing at grade any track or tracks of a railroad,","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s3","text":"to fail to completely cross the track or tracks without stopping","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s4","text":"due to insufficient: (1) Space for the vehicle on the opposite side of the railroad crossing;","role":"condition"},{"id":"s5","text":"or (2) Undercarriage clearance of the vehicle.","role":"condition"},{"id":"s6","text":"As used in this section, “completely cross” means to travel across a railroad track or tracks in such a manner that the trailing end of the vehicle is 15 feet or more past the nearest rail of the railroad track or tracks.","role":"definitional"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', less the devices it excepts), claimed as one atom and never expanded into classes. 'the driver of' names who controls that vehicle, a relational role and no membership, read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency). lines: {"node_id":"NRS_484B_560_7a","law_refs":["NRS-484B-560-7a"],"subject":{"binder":"x","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"It is unlawful for the driver of any vehicle:","role":"subject"},{"id":"s2","text":"When crossing at grade any track or tracks of a railroad,","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s3","text":"to fail to completely cross the track or tracks without stopping","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s4","text":"due to insufficient: (1) Space for the vehicle on the opposite side of the railroad crossing;","role":"condition"},{"id":"s5","text":"or (2) Undercarriage clearance of the vehicle.","role":"condition"},{"id":"s6","text":"As used in this section, “completely cross” means to travel across a railroad track or tracks in such a manner that the trailing end of the vehicle is 15 feet or more past the nearest rail of the railroad track or tracks.","role":"definitional"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', less the devices it excepts), claimed as one atom and never expanded into classes. 'the driver of' names who controls that vehicle, a relational role and no membership, read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency). The aggregate's 'not a stand-in' clause excludes a relational role as membership, which is why 'driver' claims nothing of its own."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["st.railway_crossing","rel.occupies","st.region_geometry"],"derived":[],"justification":"st.railway_crossing is the 'level crossing of a railway with the roadway, and its nearest rail': 'crossing at grade any track or tracks' is a crossing on the level. DEF-NRS-484A-200 makes a railroad 'a carrier of persons or property upon cars, other than streetcars, operated upon stationary rails'; the atom's contract is a crossing of a railway with the roadway, which a streetcar track laid along the street is not, so the definition's exclusion is already the contract's. 'When crossing' anchors the crossing to x: rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') while x is on the crossing, and st.region_geometry ('the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it') after its footprint has left it, until x has completely crossed (s6). rel.occupies is read only as overlap; st.region_geometry's 'not a stand-in for occupancy' is respected, since the distance is read only past the crossing, beside the occupancy that x had before."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["st.railway_crossing","rel.occupies","st.region_geometry","dev.human_direction","dev.governs","st.travel_region","prim.closest_approach_within","prim.closest_approach_distance"],"derived":["drv.motion.stopped"],"justification":"'without stopping' is read with DEF-NRS-484A-260, the definition that applies: 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not' is drv.motion.stopped, the halt at one observation, which denotes the halt 'whoever or whatever controls the road user' and holds at a momentary halt because it reads the one observation. The definition's exclusions are not the concept's and the rule carries them beside it: 'except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic' by prim.closest_approach_within and prim.closest_approach_distance, another road user's predicted closest approach to x within the conflict horizon coming within the conflict clearance; 'in compliance with the directions of a police officer' by dev.human_direction ('a person directing traffic and the direction given', role police_officer, indication stop) governing (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') a travel region (st.travel_region) x occupies (rel.occupies). dev.governs' 'not a stand-in for a position' is respected: it is read only as which region the officer's direction controls. 'fail to completely cross the track or tracks' reads the crossing of s2 and the law's own definition (s6): the halt is forbidden while x is on the crossing (rel.occupies) or less than the stated distance past it (st.region_geometry)."},{"span":"s4","atoms":["rel.bearing","rel.surface_gap"],"derived":[],"justification":"'due to insufficient ... Space for the vehicle on the opposite side' states why the halt happens and is read through the conduct it explains (observable_reading, purpose): x halts with another road user directly ahead of it, the one taking the space beyond the crossing. rel.bearing is the 'direction of b from a in a's frame', whose longitudinal component positive places y ahead of x, on the side toward which x crosses; rel.surface_gap, the 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies', at most the queue standstill gap says x stands at the back of y as a queued vehicle does, so the space x needed is taken. rel.surface_gap has no 'not a stand-in' clause; rel.bearing is read as a direction, not a distance. The words name no class for what fills the space, so y is any road user other than x."},{"span":"s6","atoms":["st.railway_crossing","st.region_geometry","rel.occupies"],"derived":[],"justification":"The law's own definition of 'completely cross': 'the trailing end of the vehicle is 15 feet or more past the nearest rail'. st.region_geometry gives 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it', so once x is past the crossing its body's nearest point to the crossing, the trailing end, is at least the stated literal from the crossing's boundary; 'past' is read as x having occupied the crossing (rel.occupies) and left it without the distance reaching the literal since, so the trailing end lies beyond the crossing on the side x crossed to. st.railway_crossing carries the crossing 'and its nearest rail', the boundary the distance is read to (reading on s3)."}],"operationalizations":[],"assumptions":[{"span":"s5","id":"asm.undercarriage_grounded","meaning":"The underside of the road user's vehicle touches, or lacks the clearance to pass over, the surface it is travelling across at the observation."}],"intentions":[],"compositions":[],"residues":[],"binders":[{"name":"x","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}],"applicability":"x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) crossing a railway crossing at grade: there is a railway crossing r (st.railway_crossing) whose region x's footprint overlaps at the observation (rel.occupies), or overlapped at an earlier observation with x's body less than the s6 literal (15 ft) from r (st.region_geometry distance) at every observation since that one: since(distance(x, r) < 15 ft, occupies(x, r)). A vehicle that halts short of a crossing it has not entered is not crossing; one whose body has reached the literal distance past the crossing has completely crossed and is no longer crossing.","obligation":"Violated at an observation where, for a railway crossing r selected as in the applicability (bound again in the obligation with the whole selection: the crossing x occupies, or occupied with its body less than the literal from it at every observation since), x is halted (drv.motion.stopped, tolerance p.motion_speed_tolerance) and the halt is due to an insufficiency the words name: (1) some road user y other than x lies ahead of x (rel.bearing from x to y, longitudinal component positive) with the gap between their bodies (rel.surface_gap) at most p.queue_standstill_gap, or (2) the declared assumption asm.undercarriage_grounded holds; unless the halt is one the stopping definition excludes: some road user z other than x has a predicted closest approach to x within p.conflict_time_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance), or a dev.human_direction with role police_officer and indication stop governs (dev.governs) a travel region (st.travel_region) x occupies (rel.occupies). Compliant at every other observation of the crossing: crossing without halting, or halting only once completely across, meets the duty. Where x is halted on the crossing with no road user ahead within the gap and the assumption undeclared, the cause of the halt is unknown and so is the verdict.","params":["p.motion_speed_tolerance","p.queue_standstill_gap","p.conflict_time_horizon","p.conflict_centre_clearance"],"narrowings":[{"span":"s1","why":"'the driver of any vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"agency"},{"span":"s4","why":"'due to insufficient ... Space' states why the halt happens; it is read through the conduct it explains, the halt directly behind a road user standing ahead within the queue standstill gap, not through a cause the trace cannot show.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"purpose"},{"span":"s3","why":"'the nearest rail' is read as the rail nearest the vehicle's trailing end once it has crossed, the edge of the crossing region on the side it crosses to, so a vehicle whose body is still on a further track has not completely crossed; the distance is read to the crossing region's boundary as the source maps it.","kind":"reading"},{"span":"s3","why":"The stopping definition's exclusion 'in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device' is read for the officer only: a device directs a halt at the place it marks (its stop line, or short of the crossing), and a halt on the tracks or less than the stated distance past them is not at such a place, so no device's indication excuses it; 'other traffic' in the definition is read as every other road user of the scene.","kind":"reading"}],"scenarios":[{"name":"forbid","expected":"violated","narrative":"x, a car, enters a level crossing; a truck y stands queued just beyond it. x halts behind y with its body still on the tracks, the gap to y within the standstill gap; no officer directs traffic and no road user moves toward x."},{"name":"permit","expected":"compliant","narrative":"x, alone in the scene, drives over a level crossing at a steady speed and continues well past it without halting."},{"name":"idle","expected":"not_applicable","narrative":"x drives on a road with no railway crossing and halts behind a queued vehicle."},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"x halts on the crossing with a vehicle y ahead of it; the source declares rel.surface_gap absent and the trace declares no undercarriage assumption, so whether x halts at the back of a queue is unknown.","masked":["rel.surface_gap"]},{"name":"branch_1","expected":"compliant","narrative":"x crosses without halting and halts behind queued y only once its body is farther than the stated distance past the crossing."},{"name":"branch_2","expected":"violated","narrative":"x halts on the crossing with no road user ahead of it; the trace declares asm.undercarriage_grounded for x at that observation."},{"name":"branch_3","expected":"compliant","narrative":"As in forbid, but a police officer at the crossing directs x to stop (dev.human_direction, role police_officer, indication stop, governing the lane x occupies) when it halts."}],"literals":[{"span":"s6","text":"15 feet","value":15,"unit":"ft"}],"param_proposals":[],"gaps":[]}

-{"concept_id":"drv.motion.stopping_distance","kind":"quantity","contract":"The distance a road user would travel from the observation to a halt if it kept its current speed for a reaction time and then slowed at a constant deceleration: its speed at the observation (kin.speed) times `reaction_time`, plus the square of that speed divided by twice `decel`, in metres along its path. It is a quantity of the road user's own motion at the one observation, whoever or whatever controls it, and is zero for a road user standing still. {"concept_id":"drv.motion.stopping_distance","kind":"quantity","contract":"The distance a road user would travel from the observation to a halt if it kept its current speed for a reaction time and then slowed at a constant deceleration: its speed at the observation (kin.speed) times `reaction_time`, plus the square of that speed divided by twice `decel`, in metres along its path. Not denoted: the distance an actual later halt takes; the grade or the surface, which the caller states through the deceleration it passes.","definition":null,"args":[{"name":"x","sort":"track"}],"params":[{"name":"reaction_time","unit":"s","meaning":"the time the road user keeps its speed before it begins to slow"},{"name":"decel","unit":"m/s^2","meaning":"the constant rate at which it slows once it begins to; strictly positive"}],"elements":[{"span":"its speed at the observation (kin.speed)","atoms":["kin.speed"],"concepts":[],"justification":"kin.speed is the 'magnitude of velocity' in m/s; the distance to a halt depends on that magnitude alone, so neither the direction of motion nor the heading is read."}],"residues":[],"literals":[{"value":2,"unit":"count","why":"The kinematic factor of constant deceleration: the distance to halt from a speed is the square of the speed over twice the deceleration."}],"scenarios":[{"name":"holds","expected":"compliant","narrative":"A road user moves at a steady speed; the instance's bounds bracket its speed times the reaction time plus the square of its speed over twice the deceleration, read at that observation."},{"name":"fails","expected":"violated","narrative":"The same road user; the instance's bounds lie wholly below the value the contract computes."},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"The source declares kin.speed absent; the value is unknown.","masked":["kin.speed"]}],"used_by":["NRS_484B_600_1a","NRS_484D_215_1_o1"],"supersedes":null}

Traffic: time-headway convention, the speed times the minimum time headway within the gap to each road user of the traffic ahead in the lane. Other highway conditions: the lateral acceleration in a bend (speed squared times st.curvature) within the acceleration the surface sustains. Width: time-to-line-crossing convention, the speed times the lateral margin needed per unit of speed within the free lateral margin, half of the lane width less the vehicle width. (1) SD is at most the sight distance at x's place (st.sight_distance) and at most the visibility distance (env.visibility). (2) For every road user y of the traffic (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) that is ahead of x in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane), x's speed times p.following_min_time_headway is at most the gap between their bodies (rel.surface_gap). (3) x's speed squared times the curvature at x's place (st.curvature) is at most a, selected as above. (4) For every lane l (st.lane) x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), x's speed times p.lane_keeping_margin_per_speed is at most half of the difference between the lane's width (st.lane_width) and x's width (kin.extent, width). lines: {"node_id":"NRS_484B_560_7a","law_refs":["NRS-484B-560-7a"],"subject":{"binder":"x","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"It is unlawful for the driver of any vehicle:","role":"subject"},{"id":"s2","text":"When crossing at grade any track or tracks of a railroad,","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s3","text":"to fail to completely cross the track or tracks without stopping","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s4","text":"due to insufficient: (1) Space for the vehicle on the opposite side of the railroad crossing;","role":"condition"},{"id":"s5","text":"or (2) Undercarriage clearance of the vehicle.","role":"condition"},{"id":"s6","text":"As used in this section, “completely cross” means to travel across a railroad track or tracks in such a manner that the trailing end of the vehicle is 15 feet or more past the nearest rail of the railroad track or tracks.","role":"definitional"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', less the devices it excepts), claimed as one atom and never expanded into classes. 'the driver of' names who controls that vehicle, a relational role and no membership, read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency). The aggregate's 'not a stand-in' clause excludes a relational role as membership, which is why 'driver' claims nothing of its own."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["st.railway_crossing","rel.occupies","st.region_geometry"],"derived":[],"justification":"st.railway_crossing is the 'level crossing of a railway with the roadway, and its nearest rail': 'crossing at grade any track or tracks' is a crossing on the level. DEF-NRS-484A-200 makes a railroad 'a carrier of persons or property upon cars, other than streetcars, operated upon stationary rails'; the atom's contract is a crossing of a railway with the roadway, which a streetcar track laid along the street is not, so the definition's exclusion is already the contract's. 'When crossing' anchors the crossing to x: rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') while x is on the crossing, and st.region_geometry ('the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it') after its footprint has left it, until x has completely crossed (s6). rel.occupies is read only as overlap; st.region_geometry's 'not a stand-in for occupancy' is respected, since the distance is read only past the crossing, beside the occupancy that x had before."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["st.railway_crossing","rel.occupies","st.region_geometry","dev.human_direction","dev.governs","st.travel_region","prim.closest_approach_within","prim.closest_approach_distance"],"derived":["drv.motion.stopped"],"justification":"'without stopping' is read with DEF-NRS-484A-260, the definition that applies: 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not' is drv.motion.stopped, the halt at one observation, which denotes the halt 'whoever or whatever controls the road user' and holds at a momentary halt because it reads the one observation. The definition's exclusions are not the concept's and the rule carries them beside it: 'except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic' by prim.closest_approach_within and prim.closest_approach_distance, another road user's predicted closest approach to x within the conflict horizon coming within the conflict clearance; 'in compliance with the directions of a police officer' by dev.human_direction ('a person directing traffic and the direction given', role police_officer, indication stop) governing (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') a travel region (st.travel_region) x occupies (rel.occupies). dev.governs' 'not a stand-in for a position' is respected: it is read only as which region the officer's direction controls. 'fail to completely cross the track or tracks' reads the crossing of s2 and the law's own definition (s6): the halt is forbidden while x is on the crossing (rel.occupies) or less than the stated distance past it (st.region_geometry)."},{"span":"s4","atoms":["rel.bearing","rel.surface_gap"],"derived":[],"justification":"'due to insufficient ... Space for the vehicle on the opposite side' states why the halt happens and is read through the conduct it explains (observable_reading, purpose): x halts with another road user directly ahead of it, the one taking the space beyond the crossing. rel.bearing is the 'direction of b from a in a's frame', whose longitudinal component positive places y ahead of x, on the side toward which x crosses; rel.surface_gap, the 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies', at most the queue standstill gap says x stands at the back of y as a queued vehicle does, so the space x needed is taken. rel.surface_gap has no 'not a stand-in' clause; rel.bearing is read as a direction, not a distance. The words name no class for what fills the space, so y is any road user other than x."},{"span":"s6","atoms":["st.railway_crossing","st.region_geometry","rel.occupies"],"derived":[],"justification":"The law's own definition of 'completely cross': 'the trailing end of the vehicle is 15 feet or more past the nearest rail'. st.region_geometry gives 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it', so once x is past the crossing its body's nearest point to the crossing, the trailing end, is at least the stated literal from the crossing's boundary; 'past' is read as x having occupied the crossing (rel.occupies) and left it without the distance reaching the literal since, so the trailing end lies beyond the crossing on the side x crossed to. st.railway_crossing carries the crossing 'and its nearest rail', the boundary the distance is read to (reading on s3)."}],"operationalizations":[],"assumptions":[{"span":"s5","id":"asm.undercarriage_grounded","meaning":"The underside of the road user's vehicle touches, or lacks the clearance to pass over, the surface it is travelling across at the observation."}],"intentions":[],"compositions":[],"residues":[],"binders":[{"name":"x","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}],"applicability":"x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) crossing a railway crossing at grade: there is a railway crossing r (st.railway_crossing) whose region x's footprint overlaps at the observation (rel.occupies), or overlapped at an earlier observation with x's body less than the s6 literal (15 ft) from r (st.region_geometry distance) at every observation since that one: since(distance(x, r) < 15 ft, occupies(x, r)). A vehicle that halts short of a crossing it has not entered is not crossing; one whose body has reached the literal distance past the crossing has completely crossed and is no longer crossing.","obligation":"Violated at an observation where, for a railway crossing r selected as in the applicability (bound again in the obligation with the whole selection: the crossing x occupies, or occupied with its body less than the literal from it at every observation since), x is halted (drv.motion.stopped, tolerance p.motion_speed_tolerance) and the halt is due to an insufficiency the words name: (1) some road user y other than x lies ahead of x (rel.bearing from x to y, longitudinal component positive) with the gap between their bodies (rel.surface_gap) at most p.queue_standstill_gap, or (2) the declared assumption asm.undercarriage_grounded holds; unless the halt is one the stopping definition excludes: some road user z other than x has a predicted closest approach to x within p.conflict_time_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance), or a dev.human_direction with role police_officer and indication stop governs (dev.governs) a travel region (st.travel_region) x occupies (rel.occupies). Compliant at every other observation of the crossing: crossing without halting, or halting only once completely across, meets the duty. Where x is halted on the crossing with no road user ahead within the gap and the assumption undeclared, the cause of the halt is unknown and so is the verdict.","params":["p.motion_speed_tolerance","p.queue_standstill_gap","p.conflict_time_horizon","p.conflict_centre_clearance"],"narrowings":[{"span":"s1","why":"'the driver of any vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"agency"},{"span":"s4","why":"'due to insufficient ... Space' states why the halt happens; it is read through the conduct it explains, the halt directly behind a road user standing ahead within the queue standstill gap, not through a cause the trace cannot show.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"purpose"},{"span":"s3","why":"'the nearest rail' is read as the rail nearest the vehicle's trailing end once it has crossed, the edge of the crossing region on the side it crosses to, so a vehicle whose body is still on a further track has not completely crossed; the distance is read to the crossing region's boundary as the source maps it.","kind":"reading"},{"span":"s3","why":"The stopping definition's exclusion 'in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device' is read for the officer only: a device directs a halt at the place it marks (its stop line, or short of the crossing), and a halt on the tracks or less than the stated distance past them is not at such a place, so no device's indication excuses it; 'other traffic' in the definition is read as every other road user of the scene.","kind":"reading"}],"scenarios":[{"name":"forbid","expected":"violated","narrative":"x, a car, enters a level crossing; a truck y stands queued just beyond it. x halts behind y with its body still on the tracks, the gap to y within the standstill gap; no officer directs traffic and no road user moves toward x."},{"name":"permit","expected":"compliant","narrative":"x, alone in the scene, drives over a level crossing at a steady speed and continues well past it without halting."},{"name":"idle","expected":"not_applicable","narrative":"x drives on a road with no railway crossing and halts behind a queued vehicle."},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"x halts on the crossing with a vehicle y ahead of it; the source declares rel.surface_gap absent and the trace declares no undercarriage assumption, so whether x halts at the back of a queue is unknown.","masked":["rel.surface_gap"]},{"name":"branch_1","expected":"compliant","narrative":"x crosses without halting and halts behind queued y only once its body is farther than the stated distance past the crossing."},{"name":"branch_2","expected":"violated","narrative":"x halts on the crossing with no road user ahead of it; the trace declares asm.undercarriage_grounded for x at that observation."},{"name":"branch_3","expected":"compliant","narrative":"As in forbid, but a police officer at the crossing directs x to stop (dev.human_direction, role police_officer, indication stop, governing the lane x occupies) when it halts."}],"literals":[{"span":"s6","text":"15 feet","value":15,"unit":"ft"}],"param_proposals":[{"name":"p.motion_speed_tolerance","unit":"m/s","value":0.2,"convention":"Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.","source":"Speed-noise floor of tracked-object kinematics in the acquisition standard"},{"name":"p.queue_standstill_gap","unit":"m","value":4.0,"convention":"Standstill gap of queued vehicles: the clearance between a vehicle halted in a queue and the one ahead of it.","source":"Car-following models' standstill (jam) distance, e.g. the Intelligent Driver Model and Wiedemann"},{"name":"p.conflict_time_horizon","unit":"s","value":3.0,"convention":"Time-to-collision horizon of the traffic-conflict technique: a predicted closest approach within this time counts as an imminent conflict.","source":"Traffic Conflict Technique (Hydén 1987), time-to-collision thresholds"},{"name":"p.conflict_centre_clearance","unit":"m","value":4.0,"convention":"Centre-to-centre distance at the predicted closest approach below which two road users' bodies come into conflict: about the sum of two passenger-car half-lengths.","source":"Design passenger-car dimensions (AASHTO Green Book design vehicle)"}],"gaps":[]}

'any person' names who controls the vehicle, a role read through the vehicle's conduct (observable_reading, agency)."},{"span":"b2","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"'a vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', less the devices it excepts), one atom, never expanded; 'of any kind or character' adds no class beyond the definition's."}],"operationalizations":[{"span":"b3","standard":"A rate of speed greater than is reasonable or proper, having due regard for the traffic, surface and width of the highway, the weather and other highway conditions","concepts":["kin.speed","drv.motion.stopping_distance","ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic","rel.ahead_behind_in_lane","rel.surface_gap","env.wet_road","env.ice_or_snow","env.precipitation","env.visibility","st.sight_distance","st.curvature","st.lane","st.lane_width","rel.occupies","kin.extent"],"params":["p.perception_reaction_time","p.surface_friction_accel_dry","p.surface_friction_accel_wet","p.surface_friction_accel_ice_or_snow","p.following_min_time_headway","p.lane_keeping_margin_per_speed"],"convention":"Stopping-sight-distance model (AASHTO Green Book): a speed is reasonable only where the vehicle can halt, after a perception-reaction time and at the deceleration the surface sustains, within the distance it can see along the road (st.sight_distance) and through the air (env.visibility); the surface selects that deceleration (ice or snow, else a wet road or falling precipitation, else dry). Traffic: time-headway convention, the speed times the minimum time headway within the gap to each road user of the traffic ahead in the lane. Other highway conditions: the lateral acceleration in a bend (speed squared times st.curvature) within the acceleration the surface sustains. Width: time-to-line-crossing convention, the speed times the lateral margin needed per unit of speed within the free lateral margin, half of the lane width less the vehicle width. Each measured magnitude enters its bound, so the bound moves with the speed, the gap, the distances, the curvature and the width; the surface condition selects among bounds.","surrogate":true}],"assumptions":[],"intentions":[],"compositions":[],"residues":[],"binders":[{"name":"x","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}],"applicability":"x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) that is being driven: x is in motion (drv.motion.moving, tolerance p.motion_speed_tolerance).","obligation":"Surrogate. At the observation x's speed (kin.speed) meets every bound the factors set. Let a be the surface's deceleration: p.surface_friction_accel_ice_or_snow where env.ice_or_snow holds, else p.surface_friction_accel_wet where env.wet_road or env.precipitation holds, else p.surface_friction_accel_dry; the stopping distance SD is drv.motion.stopping_distance(x; p.perception_reaction_time, a), written as a Term.cond over the three calls, each with its own constant parameter. (1) SD is at most the sight distance at x's place (st.sight_distance) and at most the visibility distance (env.visibility). (2) For every road user y of the traffic (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-285::traffic) that is ahead of x in the same lane (rel.ahead_behind_in_lane), x's speed times p.following_min_time_headway is at most the gap between their bodies (rel.surface_gap). (3) x's speed squared times the curvature at x's place (st.curvature) is at most a, selected as above. (4) For every lane l (st.lane) x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), x's speed times p.lane_keeping_margin_per_speed is at most half of the difference between the lane's width (st.lane_width) and x's width (kin.extent, width). Violated where any bound fails.","params":["p.motion_speed_tolerance","p.perception_reaction_time","p.surface_friction_accel_dry","p.surface_friction_accel_wet","p.surface_friction_accel_ice_or_snow","p.following_min_time_headway","p.lane_keeping_margin_per_speed"],"narrowings":[{"span":"b1","why":"'any person to drive or operate' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, whoever or whatever controls it.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"agency"},{"span":"b3","why":"'the traffic' is read only through the road users of the traffic ahead of x in its own lane, by the time headway to each; oncoming, crossing and adjacent-lane traffic, and traffic on a way with no mapped lane, set no bound.","kind":"reading"},{"span":"b3","why":"'surface' is read through env.wet_road and env.ice_or_snow, which select the deceleration; where x occupies no mapped lane the width sets no bound.","kind":"reading"},{"span":"b3","why":"'the weather' is read through env.visibility, by its degree, and env.precipitation, which selects the wet deceleration; {"concept_id":"drv.motion.stopping_distance","kind":"quantity","contract":"The distance a road user would travel from the observation to a halt if it kept its current speed for a reaction time and then slowed at a constant deceleration: its speed at the observation (kin.speed) times `reaction_time`, plus the square of that speed divided by twice `decel`, in metres along its path. It is a quantity of the road user's own motion at the one observation, whoever or whatever controls it, and is zero for a road user standing still. Not denoted: the distance an actual later halt takes; the grade or the surface, which the caller states through the deceleration it passes.","definition":null,"args":[{"name":"x","sort":"track"}],"params":[{"name":"reaction_time","unit":"s","meaning":"the time the road user keeps its speed before it begins to slow"},{"name":"decel","unit":"m/s^2","meaning":"the constant rate at which it slows once it begins to; strictly positive"}],"elements":[{"span":"its speed at the observation (kin.speed)","atoms":["kin.speed"],"concepts":[],"justification":"kin.speed is the 'magnitude of velocity' in m/s; the distance to a halt depends on that magnitude alone, so neither the direction of motion nor the heading is read."}],"residues":[],"literals":[{"value":2,"unit":"count","why":"The kinematic factor of constant deceleration: the distance to halt from a speed is the square of the speed over twice the deceleration."}],"scenarios":[{"name":"holds","expected":"compliant","narrative":"A road user moves at a steady speed; the instance's bounds bracket its speed times the reaction time plus the square of its speed over twice the deceleration, read at that observation."},{"name":"fails","expected":"violated","narrative":"The same road user; the instance's bounds lie wholly below the value the contract computes."},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"The source declares kin.speed absent; the value is unknown.","masked":["kin.speed"]}],"used_by":["NRS_484B_600_1a","NRS_484D_215_1_o1"],"supersedes":null}

lines: {"node_id":"NRS_484B_560_7a","law_refs":["NRS-484B-560-7a"],"subject":{"binder":"x","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]},"segmentation":[{"id":"s1","text":"It is unlawful for the driver of any vehicle:","role":"subject"},{"id":"s2","text":"When crossing at grade any track or tracks of a railroad,","role":"trigger"},{"id":"s3","text":"to fail to completely cross the track or tracks without stopping","role":"obligation"},{"id":"s4","text":"due to insufficient: (1) Space for the vehicle on the opposite side of the railroad crossing;","role":"condition"},{"id":"s5","text":"or (2) Undercarriage clearance of the vehicle.","role":"condition"},{"id":"s6","text":"As used in this section, “completely cross” means to travel across a railroad track or tracks in such a manner that the trailing end of the vehicle is 15 feet or more past the nearest rail of the railroad track or tracks.","role":"definitional"}],"elements":[{"span":"s1","atoms":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"],"derived":[],"justification":"'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', less the devices it excepts), claimed as one atom and never expanded into classes. 'the driver of' names who controls that vehicle, a relational role and no membership, read through the vehicle's controlled motion (observable_reading, agency). The aggregate's 'not a stand-in' clause excludes a relational role as membership, which is why 'driver' claims nothing of its own."},{"span":"s2","atoms":["st.railway_crossing","rel.occupies","st.region_geometry"],"derived":[],"justification":"st.railway_crossing is the 'level crossing of a railway with the roadway, and its nearest rail': 'crossing at grade any track or tracks' is a crossing on the level. DEF-NRS-484A-200 makes a railroad 'a carrier of persons or property upon cars, other than streetcars, operated upon stationary rails'; the atom's contract is a crossing of a railway with the roadway, which a streetcar track laid along the street is not, so the definition's exclusion is already the contract's. 'When crossing' anchors the crossing to x: rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') while x is on the crossing, and st.region_geometry ('the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it') after its footprint has left it, until x has completely crossed (s6). rel.occupies is read only as overlap; st.region_geometry's 'not a stand-in for occupancy' is respected, since the distance is read only past the crossing, beside the occupancy that x had before."},{"span":"s3","atoms":["st.railway_crossing","rel.occupies","st.region_geometry","dev.human_direction","dev.governs","st.travel_region","prim.closest_approach_within","prim.closest_approach_distance"],"derived":["drv.motion.stopped"],"justification":"'without stopping' is read with DEF-NRS-484A-260, the definition that applies: 'any halting, even momentarily, of a vehicle, whether occupied or not' is drv.motion.stopped, the halt at one observation, which denotes the halt 'whoever or whatever controls the road user' and holds at a momentary halt because it reads the one observation. The definition's exclusions are not the concept's and the rule carries them beside it: 'except when necessary to avoid conflict with other traffic' by prim.closest_approach_within and prim.closest_approach_distance, another road user's predicted closest approach to x within the conflict horizon coming within the conflict clearance; 'in compliance with the directions of a police officer' by dev.human_direction ('a person directing traffic and the direction given', role police_officer, indication stop) governing (dev.governs, 'the travel regions whose traffic the device controls') a travel region (st.travel_region) x occupies (rel.occupies). dev.governs' 'not a stand-in for a position' is respected: it is read only as which region the officer's direction controls. 'fail to completely cross the track or tracks' reads the crossing of s2 and the law's own definition (s6): the halt is forbidden while x is on the crossing (rel.occupies) or less than the stated distance past it (st.region_geometry)."},{"span":"s4","atoms":["rel.bearing","rel.surface_gap"],"derived":[],"justification":"'due to insufficient ... Space for the vehicle on the opposite side' states why the halt happens and is read through the conduct it explains (observable_reading, purpose): x halts with another road user directly ahead of it, the one taking the space beyond the crossing. rel.bearing is the 'direction of b from a in a's frame', whose longitudinal component positive places y ahead of x, on the side toward which x crosses; rel.surface_gap, the 'distance between the nearest points of two bodies', at most the queue standstill gap says x stands at the back of y as a queued vehicle does, so the space x needed is taken. rel.surface_gap has no 'not a stand-in' clause; rel.bearing is read as a direction, not a distance. The words name no class for what fills the space, so y is any road user other than x."},{"span":"s6","atoms":["st.railway_crossing","st.region_geometry","rel.occupies"],"derived":[],"justification":"The law's own definition of 'completely cross': 'the trailing end of the vehicle is 15 feet or more past the nearest rail'. st.region_geometry gives 'the ground distance from a road user's body outline to it', so once x is past the crossing its body's nearest point to the crossing, the trailing end, is at least the stated literal from the crossing's boundary; 'past' is read as x having occupied the crossing (rel.occupies) and left it without the distance reaching the literal since, so the trailing end lies beyond the crossing on the side x crossed to. st.railway_crossing carries the crossing 'and its nearest rail', the boundary the distance is read to (reading on s3)."}],"operationalizations":[],"assumptions":[{"span":"s5","id":"asm.undercarriage_grounded","meaning":"The underside of the road user's vehicle touches, or lacks the clearance to pass over, the surface it is travelling across at the observation."}],"intentions":[],"compositions":[],"residues":[],"binders":[{"name":"x","class_elements":["ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle"]}],"applicability":"x is a vehicle (ru.aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) crossing a railway crossing at grade: there is a railway crossing r (st.railway_crossing) whose region x's footprint overlaps at the observation (rel.occupies), or overlapped at an earlier observation with x's body less than the s6 literal (15 ft) from r (st.region_geometry distance) at every observation since that one: since(distance(x, r) < 15 ft, occupies(x, r)). A vehicle that halts short of a crossing it has not entered is not crossing; one whose body has reached the literal distance past the crossing has completely crossed and is no longer crossing.","obligation":"Violated at an observation where, for a railway crossing r selected as in the applicability (bound again in the obligation with the whole selection: the crossing x occupies, or occupied with its body less than the literal from it at every observation since), x is halted (drv.motion.stopped, tolerance p.motion_speed_tolerance) and the halt is due to an insufficiency the words name: (1) some road user y other than x lies ahead of x (rel.bearing from x to y, longitudinal component positive) with the gap between their bodies (rel.surface_gap) at most p.queue_standstill_gap, or (2) the declared assumption asm.undercarriage_grounded holds; unless the halt is one the stopping definition excludes: some road user z other than x has a predicted closest approach to x within p.conflict_time_horizon (prim.closest_approach_within) at a centre distance below p.conflict_centre_clearance (prim.closest_approach_distance), or a dev.human_direction with role police_officer and indication stop governs (dev.governs) a travel region (st.travel_region) x occupies (rel.occupies). Compliant at every other observation of the crossing: crossing without halting, or halting only once completely across, meets the duty. Where x is halted on the crossing with no road user ahead within the gap and the assumption undeclared, the cause of the halt is unknown and so is the verdict.","params":["p.motion_speed_tolerance","p.queue_standstill_gap","p.conflict_time_horizon","p.conflict_centre_clearance"],"narrowings":[{"span":"s1","why":"'the driver of any vehicle' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the duty binds the vehicle's conduct whoever or whatever controls it.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"agency"},{"span":"s4","why":"'due to insufficient ... Space' states why the halt happens; it is read through the conduct it explains, the halt directly behind a road user standing ahead within the queue standstill gap, not through a cause the trace cannot show.","kind":"observable_reading","category":"purpose"},{"span":"s3","why":"'the nearest rail' is read as the rail nearest the vehicle's trailing end once it has crossed, the edge of the crossing region on the side it crosses to, so a vehicle whose body is still on a further track has not completely crossed; the distance is read to the crossing region's boundary as the source maps it.","kind":"reading"},{"span":"s3","why":"The stopping definition's exclusion 'in compliance with the directions of a police officer or official traffic-control device' is read for the officer only: a device directs a halt at the place it marks (its stop line, or short of the crossing), and a halt on the tracks or less than the stated distance past them is not at such a place, so no device's indication excuses it; 'other traffic' in the definition is read as every other road user of the scene.","kind":"reading"}],"scenarios":[{"name":"forbid","expected":"violated","narrative":"x, a car, enters a level crossing; a truck y stands queued just beyond it. x halts behind y with its body still on the tracks, the gap to y within the standstill gap; no officer directs traffic and no road user moves toward x."},{"name":"permit","expected":"compliant","narrative":"x, alone in the scene, drives over a level crossing at a steady speed and continues well past it without halting."},{"name":"idle","expected":"not_applicable","narrative":"x drives on a road with no railway crossing and halts behind a queued vehicle."},{"name":"blind","expected":"unknown","narrative":"x halts on the crossing with a vehicle y ahead of it; the source declares rel.surface_gap absent and the trace declares no undercarriage assumption, so whether x halts at the back of a queue is unknown.","masked":["rel.surface_gap"]},{"name":"branch_1","expected":"compliant","narrative":"x crosses without halting and halts behind queued y only once its body is farther than the stated distance past the crossing."},{"name":"branch_2","expected":"violated","narrative":"x halts on the crossing with no road user ahead of it; the trace declares asm.undercarriage_grounded for x at that observation."},{"name":"branch_3","expected":"compliant","narrative":"As in forbid, but a police officer at the crossing directs x to stop (dev.human_direction, role police_officer, indication stop, governing the lane x occupies) when it halts."}],"literals":[{"span":"s6","text":"15 feet","value":15,"unit":"ft"}],"param_proposals":[{"name":"p.motion_speed_tolerance","unit":"m/s","value":0.2,"convention":"Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.","source":"Speed-noise floor of tracked-object kinematics in the acquisition standard"},{"name":"p.queue_standstill_gap","unit":"m","value":4.0,"convention":"Standstill gap of queued vehicles: the clearance between a vehicle halted in a queue and the one ahead of it.","source":"Car-following models' standstill (jam) distance, e.g. the Intelligent Driver Model and Wiedemann"},{"name":"p.conflict_time_horizon","unit":"s","value":3.0,"convention":"Time-to-collision horizon of the traffic-conflict technique: a predicted closest approach within this time counts as an imminent conflict.","source":"Traffic Conflict Technique (Hydén 1987), time-to-collision thresholds"},{"name":"p.conflict_centre_clearance","unit":"m","value":4.0,"convention":"Centre-to-centre distance at the predicted closest approach below which two road users' bodies come into conflict: about the sum of two passenger-car half-lengths.","source":"Design passenger-car dimensions (AASHTO Green Book design vehicle)"}],"gaps":[]}

(3) x's speed squared times the curvature at x's place (st.curvature) is at most a, selected as above.
